fatal_errors: The proposed refractory-alloy severe-plastic-deformation and aging route does not reconstruct the CoCrFeNiTi high-energy ball-milling plus spark-plasma-sintering route.

The proposed phase constitution is a BCC matrix with ordered intermetallic precipitates, not the requested dual solid-solution FCC/BCC structure; moreover, B2 phases are treated as non-brittle despite cited evidence identifying B2 among potentially brittle secondary phases.
No evidence establishes that the proposed processing route will simultaneously produce grains below 50 nm, the claimed precipitate fraction, and greater than 10% ductility.

The falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary or precipitation strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening because it lacks composition-matched controls with independently varied grain size and precipitate state.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective of strengthening a limited-ductility multi-principal alloy and correctly invokes grain refinement, solid-solution strengthening, phase stability, and atmosphere control. It is nevertheless a substantially different materials concept from the target: HPT/ECAP plus aging replaces ball milling plus SPS, the alloy family changes from equimolar CoCrFeNiTi to refractory BCC alloys, and coherent ordered precipitates replace the target nanocrystalline 83% FCC/17% BCC solid-solution mixture. The numerical outcome also disagrees, predicting yield strength above 2000 MPa and retained ductility rather than approximately 1238 MPa yield stress with limited ductility. The cited literature supports coherent precipitation in one W-based alloy and strengthening in mechanically alloyed refractory alloys, but does not validate the full proposed route or universal suppression of brittle phases. The instability boundaries are scientifically reasonable but qualitative and do not recover the target milling-time and 900–1000 °C SPS window.
